channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Turkey's Feud Deepens Over Disagreements Regarding Israel
item.description: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev's absence from the Organization of Turkic States summit in Ankara signals a deepening feud with Turkish leader Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The dispute, initially centered on Azerbaijan's religious expression regulations, appears more complex than previously understood, embarrassing Erdogan and undermining his message of Turkic unity.

item.title: Central Asia's Power Grid Faces Winter Stress Amidst Rising Demand
item.description: Concerns are mounting in Central Asia regarding the region's capacity to meet electricity demand this winter, particularly in Kyrgyzstan, where cold weather has increased consumption. A Eurasian Development Bank study highlighted the fragility of the power grid, noting frequent overloads and bottlenecks that limit capacity during critical hours.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Key Initiatives at Organization of Turkic States Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara, focusing on deepening practical cooperation. The summit, themed "Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought and Action," included leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, and Turkmenistan, discussing current issues and future prospects.

item.title: Timur Turlov and Freedom Invest Tens of Millions in Kazakh Sports
item.description: Timur Turlov and Freedom Holding Corp. have invested tens of millions of dollars in Kazakhstani sports, focusing on youth development. The Freedom QJ League, established in 2023, received over $10.71 million in the reporting period to organize competitions for youth football teams. The company also supports professional clubs and training facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Review Hemodialysis Funding Amid Rising Kidney Disease Cases
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to review its funding for hemodialysis as over 40,000 patients suffer from chronic kidney disease. The Health Ministry aims to improve dialysis care quality, enhance early diagnosis, and optimize financing. The goal is to build an effective nephrology service from polyclinics to specialized centers.

item.title: Modern Cotton Processing Plant with 50,000 Ton Annual Capacity Opens in Zhetisay
item.description: A modern cotton processing plant with an annual capacity of 50,000 tons has opened in Zhetisay, Turkistan region. The facility, 'Birlik-E' LLC, aims to boost the region's agro-industrial potential, develop domestic production, and create new jobs. Local farmers harvested 120,000 tons of cotton this year.

item.title: Mortar Shell Explosion in Paktia Kills One Child and Injures Four Others
item.description: A mortar shell fired by Pakistani forces exploded in Paktia province, killing one child and injuring four others. The incident occurred in the Dand Patan district near the Durand Line. This follows previous Pakistani shelling incidents in Nangarhar province.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Energy Sector Embraces Private Investment for Sustainable Development
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's dialogue with energy investors marks a new phase of state-business relations. The sector has attracted $35 billion in investments and increased renewable energy share to 31% since opening to private capital. Six new projects worth $4.7 billion were signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores Spanish Expertise to Boost Agricultural Productivity
item.description: Uzbekistan is seeking to enhance agricultural productivity by improving soil quality, rationalizing water use, and adopting modern technologies, drawing on Spanish experience. A recent Uzbek-Spanish business forum discussed expanding trade, launching investment projects, and implementing advanced solutions in the agricultural sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Senate Speaker Discusses Presidential Address Priorities in Akmola Region
item.description: Yerlan Koshanov, Chairman of the People's Council of Kazakhstan, met with public representatives, labor collectives, and experts in the Akmola region. The meetings focused on explaining the priorities of the President's Address and discussing their practical implementation in the region. The Address outlines Kazakhstan's development path, economic strengthening, technological modernization, and improving citizen welfare.

item.title: Trump Believes War with Iran Will End Soon, Seeks Nuclear Guarantee
item.description: US President Donald Trump expressed his belief that the conflict with Iran will conclude shortly, though he provided no specifics on how. He emphasized the need for a guarantee that Iran will not acquire nuclear weapons. Trump had previously stated that the US would avoid striking Iran before the midterm elections.

item.title: Central Asia and Azerbaijan Discuss Strengthening Political Trust and Practical Projects
item.description: An expert-diplomatic dialogue in Tashkent focused on Central Asia and Azerbaijan's new political environment based on trust and cooperation. Discussions covered strengthening political dialogue, expanding trade and economic ties, transport connectivity, and implementing high-level initiatives. The need to move beyond common positions to joint programs for industrial cooperation and economic growth was emphasized.

item.title: Head of People's Council discusses state address priorities in Akmola region
item.description: Yerlan Koshanov, Chairman of the People's Council of Kazakhstan, met with public representatives in the Akmola region to discuss the main priorities of the Head of State's address. The address outlines Kazakhstan's development path, focusing on economic strengthening, technological modernization, and improving citizens' well-being.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Build New Boiler House in Aktau, Invest in Mangystau Infrastructure
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to construct a new boiler house in Aktau worth 48 billion tenge. Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev reviewed projects for water, heating, and electricity infrastructure modernization in the Mangystau region. Efforts include expanding the "Caspian" desalination plant and deepening water intake channels for the Mangystau Atomic Energy Complex.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 300 Million Tenge for Forest Restoration Project
item.description: Kazakhstan will spend 300 million tenge to plant 3 million coniferous trees as part of a forest restoration initiative. The project, supported by "Samruk-Kazyna" with an equal amount, aims to increase forest cover, preserve biodiversity, and enhance ecological stability.

item.title: UNHCR Warns 4.2 Million in Afghanistan Need Shelter Ahead of Harsh Winter
item.description: The UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) warns that 4.2 million people in Afghanistan will require shelter due to harsh winter conditions. A report indicates nearly a third of surveyed families lack adequate winter clothing. Many returning Afghans from Iran and Pakistan face shortages of basic necessities and assistance.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan Sign Trade Deals Worth $95 Million
item.description: Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan have reached trade agreements totaling $95 million following a trade mission in Bishkek. Kazakh companies signed deals for automotive and commercial vehicle supplies, as well as agricultural cooperation. Both nations aim to increase bilateral trade to $3 billion.

item.title: Russia offers foreign partners digital platforms and AI technologies
item.description: Russia has proposed offering its domestic digital platforms, including social networks and messengers, and adapting artificial intelligence models to foreign partners. This was discussed at the Kazan Digital Week forum, which also addressed cybersecurity challenges. The forum, attended by delegates from 70 countries, covers digitalization in various sectors.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Health Ministry to investigate discrepancies in dialysis and patient death records
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health will re-examine medical data following the discovery of discrepancies in hemodialysis and patient death records. The ministry has ordered a thorough review of cases where dialysis dates coincide with patient death dates and will revise kidney transplant protocols for children. The investigation aims to ensure the accuracy of electronic medical records.

item.title: Kazakhstan court denies defense's request to recuse judge in Bokaev case
item.description: A court in Kazakhstan has again denied the defense's request to recuse the judge in the case of civil activist Sanjar Bokaev. The defense argued the judge was biased, citing ignored objections and the judge's alleged interruption of Bokaev's questions. The prosecution countered that their questions were relevant to the charges.

item.title: New Historical Era: From Stated Goals to Concrete Results in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President's address outlines strategic development vectors and the need for paradigm shifts. The message emphasizes addressing new challenges in governance and socio-economic development, moving beyond past stereotypes. The goal is to build a competitive, stable, and high-quality state for future generations, focusing on modernizing the economic infrastructure.

item.title: North Korean Hackers Suspected in Massive Binance Crypto Exchange Breach
item.description: North Korean hackers, possibly the Lazarus Group, are suspected of stealing over $6 billion from the Binance crypto exchange. Analysts from TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the group to Russia, noting its activity within the Russian Federation and traffic routing through Russian servers. Binance believes hackers gained access by compromising an engineer's laptop.

item.title: Binance Founder Asks Elon Musk to Stop 'Trolling' Amid $6 Billion Hack
item.description: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao urged Elon Musk to cease 'trolling' following a hack that drained over $6 billion from the exchange. Zhao highlighted the value of their SPCX shares, exceeding $1 billion, and requested support. Hackers reportedly accessed the system via an engineer's laptop, with approximately $3 billion frozen and $1 billion in reserve.

item.title: Hematology Center Opens in Oskemen Using Returned State Assets
item.description: A new hematology center has opened in Oskemen, East Kazakhstan region, funded by assets returned to the state. The modern facility, with 148 beds, will provide high-tech medical care to over 720,000 residents of the region and citizens nationwide for severe blood diseases and oncological pathologies. The project fulfills the President's directive to return assets for public benefit.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Host First-Ever BRICS+ Science Week Across All Regions
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the BRICS+ Science Week from November 2nd to 8th, marking the first time the event will span all regions of the country. The V International Festival 'Science 0+' in Tashkent on November 7-8 will be a central event. The festival, part of Russia's Decade of Science and Technology, aims to promote scientific literacy and engagement.

item.title: Kazakhstan Man Arrested for Online Comment, Claims Account Was Fake
item.description: A resident of Almaty, Dmitry Borodaev, was detained for allegedly posting negative comments about Ukrainian nationalists and insulting the Kazakh language online. He claims the account used was fake and denies posting the controversial remarks. Borodaev was detained on September 29 and is suspected of inciting ethnic hatred.

item.title: Kazakhstan's "Adilet" Party Drafts Legislation Following President's Address
item.description: Kazakhstan's "Adilet" party has begun drafting legislation based on the President's address. Key initiatives include making land allocation more transparent, implementing party control over construction projects, and involving youth in infrastructure development. The party plans over 3,000 public discussions on the address.

item.title: Issyk-Kul authorities remove 1,200 meters of illegal fishing nets
item.description: The Issyk-Kul regional environmental inspection agency conducted a raid, removing approximately 1,200 meters of illegal synthetic fishing nets from the lake. Additionally, 20 kilograms of trash were collected during the operation aimed at cleaning the lake's waters.

item.title: Kazakhstan's international role and reforms discussed at Spanish university conference
item.description: A conference at IE University in Spain focused on Kazakhstan's development post-independence. The Kazakh Ambassador to Spain, Danat Musayev, highlighted the country's foreign policy, its role as a middle power, and contributions to nuclear disarmament. Economic modernization, investment potential, and the Middle Corridor transport route were also discussed.

item.title: Kazakh government rejects proposal for uniform tax rate for entrepreneurs
item.description: The Kazakh government has rejected a proposal to introduce a uniform 2-3% tax rate for entrepreneurs under a simplified declaration regime. The proposal, which also sought to remove regional authorities' power to adjust tax rates, was deemed incompatible with the new Tax Code's provisions for differentiated rates based on business activity and location.

item.title: Uzbek Citizens Invited to Work in Kuwait with Salaries Up to $2400
item.description: Uzbek citizens are being offered employment opportunities in Kuwait, with potential monthly salaries reaching $2400. Specifically, there are 10 vacancies available in the electrical engineering field. Candidates must possess higher education, at least eight years of work experience, and fluency in English.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz: Ustyurt Project with SOCAR and BP Still in Exploration Phase, No Field Discovered
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz's joint Ustyurt project with Azerbaijan's SOCAR and UK's BP is currently in the geological exploration stage, with no oil or gas field discovered yet. Seismic surveys covering over 3,000 sq km have been conducted, and drilling one well is planned for next year.

item.title: Chinese Experts Recognize Kazakhstan as Key Eurasian Link and Middle Power
item.description: Chinese experts have lauded Kazakhstan's political and socio-economic transformations, identifying the country as a middle power and a crucial link in Eurasia. They highlighted Kazakhstan's role in ensuring regional security and sustainable development during a forum in Shanghai.

item.title: Pakistani Jets Bomb Taliban Base in Afghanistan's Paktika Province
item.description: Pakistani fighter jets reportedly bombed a Taliban military base in the Shakin district of Paktika province, near the Angoor Ada border crossing. The base was reportedly abandoned by the Taliban three months prior. This incident follows several clashes between Taliban fighters and Pakistani forces along the border.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases After Four Days of Growth
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has fallen after a four-day increase. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 31. The data indicates a slight decrease in the dollar's value.

item.title: Binance Reserves Over $6.34 Billion to Cover Losses from Hacker Attack
item.description: Following a hacker attack that resulted in the theft of cryptocurrencies valued between $1.7 billion and $5.5 billion, the international crypto exchange Binance has reserved over $6.34 billion from its own funds to cover user losses. The company has begun efforts to restore assets for affected users.

item.title: New Polio Vaccination Campaign to Commence Across Afghanistan on Monday
item.description: A new round of polio vaccination campaigns is set to begin across Afghanistan on Monday, announced the Polio Free Afghanistan initiative. The campaign in the southern zone will start a day later, on Tuesday, November 3. UNICEF reports that 12.7 million children have been vaccinated so far.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Seeks Stronger Strategic Partnership with Turkey, President Japarov Meets Erdogan
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation. Japarov expressed gratitude for the warm reception and high-level organization of the Turkic States Summit. He emphasized Kyrgyzstan's interest in enhancing its comprehensive strategic partnership with Turkey, noting broad opportunities for increased interaction in mutually beneficial areas.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Initiatives on Industry, Logistics, Tourism, and Visa-Free Travel at Turkic States Summit
item.description: At the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan put forward proposals concerning industry, logistics, tourism, and visa-free travel. The summit, held under the theme "Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Action," was attended by leaders from member states and observers. Mirziyoyev expressed gratitude for Turkey's organization and highlighted the opening of a national-cultural complex.

item.title: Turkish Intelligence Captures Suspected Daesh Operative in Afghanistan-Pakistan Region
item.description: Turkey's National Intelligence Organization (MIT) has captured a suspected member of the Daesh terrorist group operating in the Afghanistan-Pakistan region. The suspect, identified as Uğur Bahadır, also known by the alias Abdullah, was allegedly involved with Daesh's Khorasan branch (ISKP). Security sources confirmed the operative has been transferred to Turkey.
